newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's NRMA eyes home loan market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's NRMA eyes home loan market.

text.p: Unlisted Australian insurance and motoring group NRMA Ltd said on Friday that it was contemplating entering the domestic home loans market.

Asked at a news conference what new services NRMA could introduce, the group's chief executive Malcom Jones said: "It was in the papers not so long ago about whether we would consider going into home loans."
Jones said the NRMA was not at the stage of introducing new services but was contemplating new areas like home loans.
"I think that we have to broaden the appeal of the NRMA name otherwise you build yourself into a corner," Jones said.

Jones said one problem NRMA had was that it was not percieved by the general public as a financial services organisation. "We want to start to broaden that appeal because we have an organisation of enormous financial strength and we are a very real alternative," he said.
Jones said NRMA needed to determine whether the home loans business was viable.
"Clearly it is quite competitive at present there is a lot of changes going on (in that market) at the moment," he said.

Entering the home loans market would also have to fit the relationship the NRMA was trying to develop with its membership base, Jones said. "We don't have answers to those particular questions at this particular time," he said.
Earlier on Friday NRMA announced a group profit after tax, abnormals and unrealised gains for the year to June 30 of A$8.8 million, compared with a loss of A$44.5 million a year earlier.
The NRMA is the dominant motor vehicle insurer in Australia's largest market, New South Wales, insuring about 30 percent of the total compulsory third party market.
